newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-RAIN MAKES EARLY FIRST APPEARANCE AT WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RAIN MAKES EARLY FIRST APPEARANCE AT WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Rain made its first appearance at the Wimbledon tennis championships on Monday, within an hour of the start of the opening day.
Defending champion Richard Krajicek and his opponent Marcello Craca had only just walked out on to Centre Court when the rain began, sending them back to the changing rooms.
On the outside courts, where the day's programme began earlier, only three matches were completed before light rain stopped play for an hour.
Men's second seed Goran Ivanisevic and the women's number 12 Irina Spirlea of Romania were among those beating the rain to reach the second round.
Play resumed on the outside courts after an hour's delay but stopped again almost immediately.
Some eight cms of rain fell at Wimbledon in the week before the championships and more is forecast for the fortnight.
The sodden ground meant one of the main car parks, on a golf course opposite the All England club, had to be closed, causing enormous traffic jams in south-west London.
Disgruntled spectators forced to leave their cars further away then faced a 40-minute wait to get into the ground as bag searches by security guards held up queues at the gates.
Security has been stepped up at Wimbledon after the Irish Republican Army (IRA) bomb scare which disrupted the Grand National horse race in April.
